newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: News Corp's Murdoch criticises Australia govt.
newsitem.headline: News Corp's Murdoch criticises Australia govt.

text.p: News Corp Ltd chief executive and chairman Rupert Murdoch has criticised the conservative government of Australian prime minister John Howard for not implementing decisive changes to boost the economy, the Courier-Mail newspaper reported on Friday.
The newspaper, owned by News Corp's News Ltd subsidiary, quoted Murdoch as saying in an interview that bold action was needed to reduce the size of government and get rid of deficits.
"More than that, take it right down so you can lower taxes and help people save money and help small business," he said.
"If you're going to make radical changes, you'd better make them in the first year," Murdoch said of the government, which defeated the Labor government in the election on March 2.
"I think they've been slow to do that and not appearing as radical a government as I would have hoped," the newspaper quoted Murdoch as saying.
Murdoch was also quoted as saying he believed the government had a complete mandate for change.
"It's a question of how much change they really want themselves or if they just want to govern quietly and change some directions," Murdoch said.
"All I know is that if this country really is going to prosper and enjoy its potential, there's got to be a lot of change," Murdoch said.

Murdoch also said he expected that cross-media ownership restrictions, which prevent a television operator owning a newspaper in the same market, would be removed. But restrictions on foreign ownership would probably remain, Murdoch said.
"That would be my best tip at the moment. We will, of course, be fighting that, putting a very strong case against that," the newspaper quoted Murdoch as saying.
